correctness.rationale: The first edge Poisson-clock reduction is exact by monotone blocking. Removing an edge factors half-lines, where terminal vacancy u(t)=exp(-(1-e^{-t})), giving p_infty(t)=e^{-t}u(t)^2. Strictly decreasing ancestral-clock paths yield uniform space-time localization with eps_R<=2^{R+2}/R!. With R=ceil(4 log n), edge indicators have O(R)-sized dependency neighborhoods, rare marginals e^{-2-x}/n+O_L(n^-2)+O(eps_R), and P(Y_e=Y_f=1)<=e^-2t for distinct edges; b1,b2=O_L(R/n), restoring coupling costs n eps_R. Mixed factorial moments with O(n^{k-1}R) nonseparated tuples give the spatial PPP. N=0 iff no future accepted deposition, so the zero-event CDF and Gumbel centering follow. Direct independent first-clock simulations at n=128 and 512 support but do not prove the limit.

originality.rationale: Classical infinite-line empty-pair probabilities, clock constructions, concentration and dependency-neighborhood Poisson bounds are prior. Materially inspected general-graph RSA treatment proves occupancy normal approximations, not the logarithmic rare-availability PPP and cyclic Gumbel jamming time; fully connected k-mer extreme-value time has a genuinely different geometry and scaling. Within inspected sources the combined spatial PPP, quantitative rate and cyclic jamming law are not shown. Historical priority remains best of knowledge only.
